name: U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz
status: President Trump told Axios (17 Sep) he faces a 'big decision' on whether to 'annihilate' Iran's regime, ahead of a Tuesday meeting with six Gulf leaders at UNGA. Iran's IRGC Navy separately claimed (18 Sep) it struck and detained the Togo-flagged tanker 'Trend' for 'illegal passage' through Hormuz; UKMTO logged a corroborating but unconfirmed incident near Khasab, Oman. Petroline restart remains unconfirmed by Aramco; Yanbu status is disputed (YASREF refinery reportedly operating normally per Industrial Info, while other reporting describes suspended port loadings). Iraq's disarmament-deadline walk-back and the Salalah ministerial postponement remain unchanged.
importance: Critical -- presidential-level escalatory rhetoric now compounds a week of CENTCOM-confirmed escalation and a new claimed maritime seizure, just as CBO quantifies the war's cost at $2-3B/month.
assessment: ASSESSED: the rhetoric escalated further this cycle without a confirmed new military action -- Tuesday's Gulf-leaders meeting is the near-term inflection point. Iranian claims (tanker seizure, prior Qeshm/MQ-9 claims) remain unconfirmed by Western sources.
lastChange: 2026-09-18 -- Trump tells Axios he faces a 'big decision' on 'annihilating' Iran; IRGC claims striking/detaining the tanker 'Trend'; Yanbu refinery-vs-port-loadings status disputed; Petroline restart still unconfirmed.
orgRelevance: Treat the current disruption level as hardening, not easing -- extend the multi-week Gulf-transiting shipping, energy, and insurance planning assumption. Watch Tuesday's Gulf-leaders meeting and any CENTCOM statement on the tanker incident.
nextIndicator: Outcome of Tuesday's Gulf-leaders meeting; independent confirmation of the 'Trend' seizure; any CENTCOM statement; Petroline partial-restoration completion; any formal Iraqi clarification of the 30 Sep deadline; a rescheduled Salalah date.

Multiple drones from Iraqi territory strike the Petroline pipeline (10-11 Sep window); Saudi Arabia shuts the line as a precaution; investigation into the Iraq launch point opens; no claim of responsibility.

A new attack near Qeshm Island strikes an Iranian commercial vessel (IRIB: 1 killed, 4 injured) and UKMTO reports a separate vessel hit by an unidentified projectile; Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince meets Iranian President Pezeshkian at the BRICS summit in New Delhi — first top-level Iran-UAE contact of the war; Iran's nuclear chief is barred from traveling to the IAEA Vienna conference.

The 14 Sep Salalah ministerial is postponed 'in the interest of consensus'; CNBC publishes satellite imagery confirming the extent of Petroline pipeline damage; a bilateral Iran-Oman shipping-lane arrangement continues to be advanced separately.

Iraq dismisses the Maysan military commander and provincial police chief after an investigation into the Petroline strikes' Iraqi origin; IRI issues a non-denial; AP reports a 3-5 week repair estimate; the Salalah ministerial collapse is confirmed to stem from a substantive Saudi objection to the Iran-Oman proposal's wording, with no reschedule date set.

Iraq's own September deadline to disarm Iran-aligned militias is identified as running in parallel with, and complicated by, the Petroline-attribution investigation into those same networks; no new repair or reschedule data this cycle.

CENTCOM confirms an attempted Iranian USV seizure after six days of silence; a REPORTED U.S. strike destroys two IRGC boats (15 Sep); Houthis claim a Yanbu refinery attack; Iraq's security advisor walks back the 30 Sep disarmament deadline; Aramco reports a ~50%-within-days / full-in-4-6-weeks Petroline restoration timeline; CBO estimates the war has cost $38B through 1 Aug ($2-3B/month ongoing).

name: Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets
status: China's State Council exit-control regulation (Decree No. 841), barring rare-earth/battery/semiconductor engineers from leaving China indefinitely with no fixed time limit, is now confirmed in force as of its 15 Sep effective date; no first enforcement case has been publicly reported. This adds a human-capital lever alongside the unchanged military-affiliated license denial (since 1 Dec 2025) and the June 2026 entity-list targeting of MP Materials/USA Rare Earth. The confirmed 23-25 Sep Xi Jinping Washington visit is now complicated by a REPORTED Chinese threat to cancel the summit if a pending $14B Taiwan arms sale is approved beforehand.
importance: Critical — binding, targeted constraint on munitions/platform output, now deepened by a talent-mobility control instrument that is independent of the summit's likely outcome, and arriving alongside new summit-cancellation risk.
assessment: The chokepoint is deepening structurally (via talent immobilization) independent of summit timing; even the realistic 'good' summit outcome would not touch either the licensing denial or the new exit-control rule, and the summit's occurrence itself is now less certain than last cycle's analyst consensus assumed. Supply-chain and technical-talent mitigation should proceed regardless.
lastChange: 2026-09-18 -- exit-control regulation now identified precisely as Decree No. 841, signed by Premier Li Qiang on 22 Jul 2026 and targeting rare-earth-separation, N-type solar, and EV-battery-electrolyte specialists; still no enforcement case reported; pre-summit commentary now frames rare earths alongside tariffs, the Taiwan arms sale, and Iran policy as simultaneous flashpoints.
orgRelevance: Continue mapping magnet exposure in hardware BOMs against named entities and pursuing second sources without waiting on summit outcomes; separately assess any PRC-based personnel, supplier, or technical-exchange exposure to the new exit-control rule, now with specific targeted specialties to check against.
nextIndicator: First reported exit-ban enforcement case; confirmation of the Taiwan arms-sale decision; any explicit rare-earth licensing signal at or around the 24 Sep summit; the 10 Nov 2026 suspension-expiry decision; any further PRC entity-list action.

name: Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / Identity / AI-Infra CVEs
status: Four new CISA KEV additions in 48 hours: Cisco Identity Services Engine (CVE-2026-76460, KEV 16 Sep), Cisco Secure Email Gateway (CVE-2026-76461, KEV 14 Sep, FCEB deadline 17 Sep), Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel/WHM (CVE-2026-87886), and a targeted Google Pixel modem flaw (CVE-2026-58704) -- a second distinct Cisco product family (identity + email) now under active exploitation alongside FMC. WSO2 API Manager (CVE-2026-5430, JWT algorithm-confusion auth bypass) shows REPORTED active exploitation via honeypot telemetry since 13 Sep, not yet KEV-listed. GitLab CVE-2026-85706 and Cisco FMC (Sandworm/Qilin) exploitation remain unresolved from prior cycles with no new named DIB-sector victim; Citrix NetScaler exploitation continues without new attribution.
importance: Critical — a recurring, multi-vendor pattern of actively exploited edge/identity infrastructure now spans at least two Cisco product families plus GitLab, with same-day federal patch deadlines and no narrowing of DIB-sector exposure.
assessment: ASSESSED: this is no longer a single-vendor, single-flaw problem -- edge and identity infrastructure broadly is the persistent intrusion vector. Prior-cycle campaigns (GitLab, FMC, NetScaler) remain live and unmitigated for unremediated organizations.
lastChange: 2026-09-18 -- no new KEV additions since 16 Sep; Cisco ISE (CVSS 10.0) and Cisco Secure Email Gateway remain unpatched/unresolved industry-wide; WSO2 API Manager confirmed still NOT KEV-listed despite ongoing REPORTED exploitation; no named DIB victim on any tracked CVE.
orgRelevance: Verify Cisco ISE and Secure Email Gateway remediation is fully closed, not merely initiated; patch WSO2 proactively regardless of KEV status; confirm GitLab and Cisco FMC remediation (patch plus any needed secrets/credential rotation) remains fully closed out.
nextIndicator: A WSO2 KEV listing; a confirmed DIB-sector or federal-contractor victim tied to any of these CVEs; further KEV adds in the same product classes; any new Citrix NetScaler attribution.

name: Ukraine Ceasefire Diplomacy / Zaporizhzhia
status: Rosatom's CEO and IAEA Director General Grossi confirmed meeting in Vienna (17 Sep) on ZNPP safety, with Rosatom describing the security situation as 'sharply deteriorated' since late April (750+ reported attacks, 20 killed). External power to ZNPP was restored after the plant lost its last remaining offsite line (Ferrosplavna-1) around 20 Aug and ran roughly a month on diesel -- a previously untracked outage distinct from the 7 Sep restoration. Strikes continued on both sides through 17 Sep with no Russian agreement to a mutual halt. Separately, Polish PM Tusk warned (18 Sep) Russia intends to stage a false-flag drone/missile incident on NATO territory to test Article 5 cohesion.
importance: High — shapes European security and munitions/air-defense demand; the energy-strike dispute now also carries direct U.S. domestic fuel-price politics, and the Tusk warning adds a distinct NATO-cohesion risk vector.
assessment: No durable halt exists. The Vienna meeting is now confirmed (resolving the prior cycle's unconfirmed report), and ZNPP's power situation is shown to be recurringly, not durably, fragile. Tusk's warning is a new, distinct alliance-cohesion signal.
lastChange: 2026-09-18 -- Rosatom-IAEA Vienna meeting confirmed; ZNPP's ~30-day power outage (from ~20 Aug) and restoration detailed; strikes continue with no Russian halt agreement; Tusk warns of Russian false-flag risk to NATO territory.
orgRelevance: Macro A&D demand context; treat any reported ceasefire as unconfirmed until both sides jointly affirm it. The expanding deep-strike campaign, fuel-market volatility, and now NATO-cohesion risk remain relevant to European energy-security and logistics-cost monitoring.
nextIndicator: Russian agreement to a mutual halt with a verification mechanism; any further ZNPP power-status change; any NATO-territory incident attributed to Russia following Tusk's warning.

name: Space Control / Orbital Weapons Disclosure
status: Following Meink's 14 Sep disclosure, China's foreign ministry expressed opposition to 'weaponisation of outer space' and Russia called for space to remain 'free of any weapons,' both around 16 Sep. A Space Force spokesperson responded that the U.S. has tracked Chinese/Russian counter-space testing since 2007 and that space is 'no longer' in question as a warfighting domain. No further U.S. technical elaboration (type, scale, timeline) has been given.
importance: High — ends a long-standing U.S. policy of deliberate ambiguity on space weapons, reframing space as a domain of open declaratory posture, and has now drawn a formal adversary reaction within 48 hours.
assessment: ASSESSED: the disclosure has moved from a one-sided U.S. statement to an active rhetorical exchange with both major adversaries, confirming the declaratory-posture shift is being read internationally as significant rather than background noise.

name: FAR Overhaul / Acquisition Reform (EO 14275)
status: The FAR Council published a proposed rule (Federal Register document 2026-19159, 18 Sep 2026) reorganizing FAR Parts 9 (contractor qualifications), 27 (patents/data rights), and 47 (transportation), implementing Executive Order 14275's 'Revolutionary FAR Overhaul.' It is the first concrete regulatory text from a previewed 12-rule simplification package. Comment period closes 19 Oct 2026.
importance: High -- governs contractor-qualification standards and IP/data-rights defaults across the DIB; further Parts in the same package are expected.
assessment: ASSESSED: a deliberate, staged rollout of FAR simplification via Part-specific proposed rules rather than a single omnibus rewrite; expect additional Parts to follow in the coming months.
